decision.topic: renew the lapsed hold silently, or warn and stop
decision.why: an agent still writing plainly still wants the hold; renewing turns the trap into a non-event (one line telling the agent it happened), and the write goes out queued instead of live. Warning-only would still leave the very next write after the warning unheld unless the agent stops to re-take it by hand -- the same failure the brief is fixing, one write later.
decision.alternative: warn only, never re-take the lock automatically -- rejected because the residual risk of renewing (an agent that truly finished and forgot to release could have some later, unrelated write to public/ silently re-arm its old hold) is smaller and more local than the risk being fixed (a live 404 the owner sees) -- and it is bounded: renewal only ever fires for a write carrying that SAME agent`s own recorded `who`, never a stranger`s, and the hold`s own 5-minute self-expiry still applies after the renewal, so it cannot stick forever either way.

log.msg: PROVEN, three real runs against the real Server/hold.mjs lock file (RELOAD_HOLD_TTL_MS=5000, per hold.mjs`s own header). Outcome 2 (never taken): check(file, `hg-test-2`) with no prior record -- printed nothing. Outcome 3 (genuinely live): took a real hold `hg-test-3`, recorded it, ran check() immediately -- status before and after both read `5s left`, untouched. Outcome 1 (lapsed): took a real hold `hg-test-1`, recorded it, slept 6s past the 5s TTL -- status read `free -- no holders` (the live dev server`s own poll loop had already pruned it, which check() also treats as lapsed since the holder is simply absent) -- ran check(), which printed {"decision":"block","reason":"RELOAD HOLD RENEWED: your hold \"hg-test-1\" had lapsed ... it has been silently re-taken for another 300s ..."}, and status afterward read `300s left` again, a fresh hold. Full transcript is this task`s own turns; nothing left held at the end (`node Server/hold.mjs` reads free).

assign.outcome: **A lapsed reload hold now renews itself and says so, instead of the agent finding out from a 404.** `.claude/hooks/hold-guard.mjs` checks, on an agent's own next write to `public/`, whether a hold it took has since lapsed — proven with three real runs against the live lock file: lapsed (silently renewed, one line printed), never taken (silent), genuinely still live (silent, untouched). The [hold-guard page](/framework/ai/2026-09-19/hold-guard/) shows the proof and the reasoning. The check half already runs today (wired into `ledger.mjs`, same as `syntax-guard.mjs`); the record half needs one new line in `.claude/settings.json` (`.claude/hooks/readme.md` spells out the exact JSON, and so does this task's log) — the owner's file, their call. Left alone on purpose: the hold's own five-minute self-expiry, unchanged — a hold that could never lapse would be a worse bug than the one this fixes.
